subject: fix(core): keep an asset's creation date across updates (#18643)
body:
An asset's `created` timestamp was reset on every update, so it always
equalled `updated` and the original registration time was lost. The
`Asset` constructor defaults `created` to now when none is given, so on
an update the incoming asset always carried a fresh timestamp and the
fallback to the stored one never fired. The stored date now wins, and
only `updated` moves forward.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/issues/10288.

subject: fix(triggers): disambiguate colliding trigger picker labels by plugin title (#18667)
body:
* fix(triggers): disambiguate colliding trigger picker labels by plugin title

The "Add Trigger" picker showed the MongoDB trigger as "Mongodb Trigger"
(wrong casing) and rendered it identically to Debezium's MongoDB CDC
trigger, since both are indistinguishable in the picker.

Root cause: PluginController#toApiTriggerPlugin always set the trigger's
`title` to `triggerClass.getSimpleName()`, which is literally "Trigger"
for the vast majority of plugins (Kestra's convention names every
plugin's trigger class `Trigger`). The frontend's triggerCatalog.ts then
fell back to guessing a label from the last Java package segment
(`trigger.type.split(".").at(-2)`) and title-casing it via
formatPluginTitle's bare capitalize() - so io.kestra.plugin.mongodb and
io.kestra.plugin.debezium.mongodb both derived "mongodb" -> "Mongodb".

Every plugin already declares a correct, human-authored title in its
metadata/index.yaml (e.g. "MongoDB", "Debezium MongoDB"), surfaced via
RegisteredPlugin#title() and already used correctly by the main Plugins
page through Plugin#of(). Reuse that same source of truth instead of
guessing from the class package:

- core: add Plugin#titleFor(RegisteredPlugin, Class), resolving an
  element's title with the same subgroup-title precedence as Plugin#of
  (subgroup's own @PluginSubGroup#title, then the owning plugin's own
  title), so it also disambiguates same-plugin subgroups correctly.
- webserver: PluginController#toApiTriggerPlugin now surfaces this as a
  new `pluginTitle` field on ApiTriggerPlugin.
- ui: triggerCatalog.ts's triggerDisplayName() falls back to the new
  `pluginTitle` field instead of deriving a guess from the class package.

This generalizes to any two plugins whose Java package happens to share
a segment, not just mongodb vs debezium-mongodb.

Relates to kestra-io/plugin-mongodb#125 and kestra-io/plugin-mongodb#124.
See also the docs-only companion PRs kestra-io/plugin-mongodb#128 and
kestra-io/plugin-debezium#210.

* test(triggers): add pluginTitle to AddTriggerModal spec fixture

subject: fix(core): fix taskRunId metric sort and share the non-sortable field list
body:
AbstractJdbcMetricRepository.sortMapping() mapped the lowercase "taskrunId",
not the "taskRunId" used everywhere else for this field (MetricEntry,
MetricController, and every other key in that same map), so sorting metrics
by sort=taskRunId:asc was rejected with a 422 while the mistyped taskrunId
silently worked.

Also extracts AbstractJdbcRepository's NON_SORTABLE_COLUMNS into a new shared
io.kestra.core.repositories.NonSortableFields.DEFAULT, so it is no longer
duplicated between the JDBC and Elasticsearch backends (kestra-ee). JDBC
derives its snake_case column names from it via camelToSnake; the derived set
is unchanged from the previous hardcoded one.

Adds two tests to the shared AbstractMetricRepositoryTest, exercised by both
the JDBC and Elasticsearch backends: sorting by "value" (kept sortable
despite being excluded elsewhere, since metrics expose it as their own
top-level field) and by "taskRunId" (regression guard for the fix above).

subject: fix(core): validate the sort query parameter against the table columns
body:
An unvalidated sort field on flows/search, logs/search and triggers/search
reached jOOQ's ORDER BY unchecked, so an unknown column produced a 500 whose
body echoed the full generated SQL, disclosing schema and query internals.

AbstractJdbcRepository.sort() now validates the field against the real
columns of the repository's table, loaded once from the database metadata
and cached, excluding a small set of internal columns (key, value, fulltext,
source_code, deleted, tenant_id, revision). An unknown or excluded field now
returns a clean 422 naming the field instead of a 500 with the SQL body.

Also fixes the trigger repository's sortMapping(), which passed unknown
fields straight through, and adds the missing updateDate->updated alias on
the KV list endpoint. Narrows TriggersManage.vue's sortable columns to drop
two fields with no backing column.

Fixes #18490

subject: fix(executions): show an empty task output instead of dropping or mangling it (#18602)
body:
* fix(executions): keep an empty task output instead of dropping it

An output whose value is an empty object or array disappeared from the Outputs
view entirely. `flatten` recurses into anything of type object, and an empty one
has no leaves to contribute, so the key was silently dropped — a script that
produced no files showed no `outputFiles` row at all, leaving no way to tell an
empty value from a missing one.

An empty container is now kept as its own value. A top-level empty object still
flattens to an empty result rather than gaining a blank key.

`flatten` has exactly one caller, `executionVars`, so the change is contained to
the Outputs view; the other `flatten` calls in the codebase are unrelated local
functions.

subject: fix(namespaces): apply a namespace file rename only once the server accepts it (#18533)
body:
* fix(namespaces): apply a namespace file rename only once the server accepts it

`renameItem` fired the rename request without awaiting it and then mutated the
tree on the next line, so the outcome was shown before the server had answered.
Renaming onto an existing name answers 500, and the tree still displayed the
rename as done until the next reload put the old name back. The call is now
awaited, the tree is touched only on success, and a failure surfaces a message
naming the attempted name.

The same function left any open tab for the file untouched. Tabs are keyed by
path, so the stale tab pointed at a path that no longer existed and clicking it
navigated to a full-page 404, dropping the user out of the editor. The tab is
now moved to the new path when the rename succeeds.

Moving the tab needs to know whether one was open, so the close handler
provided by `useFilesPanels` now reports whether it removed anything. While
adding that, its lookup went from a prefix test to an exact match on the tab
uid: uids are `code-<path>`, so closing `a.py` could close `a.python` instead
whenever the longer path was listed first. Covered by four new unit tests, two
of which fail against the prefix lookup.

`closeTab` was also injected 190 lines below its first use, relying on the
temporal dead zone never being hit; it now sits next to `openTab`.

Closes #18467
Closes #18468

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01WAUBiJTcC3ABYSnRiUiPzZ

* fix(namespaces): report a failed rename once, and block a duplicate submit

Review found the friendly error toast is a second surface, not the only one.
Every generated SDK call goes through the interceptor in `utils/kestraHttp.ts`,
which for any status other than 400/401 sets `coreStore.message` and renders it
as a non-auto-hiding ErrorToast. The backend refuses a colliding rename with a
500, so the user got a persistent raw "Internal Server Error: /path/..." next to
the readable one. The sibling drag path, `nodeMoved`, catches and shows nothing
for exactly this reason, so the precedent was the opposite of what was shipped.
`renameFileDirectory` now suppresses the global message; it is called only from
`renameItem`, and the byte-identical `moveFileDirectory` keeps the global toast
for the drag path.

Moving the dialog reset after the await also left the Rename button and the
dialog's Enter handler live while the request was in flight. The Enter handler is
not gated by the button's disabled state, so two Enters fired two renames of the
same path; the second failed because the old path was already gone, and the user
saw a failure for a rename that had actually worked. An `isRenaming` guard closes
that window and drives the button's disabled and loading states.

subject: fix(core): 500 on labels search filters that need a label key
body:
Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/issues/10150.

filters[labels][EQUALS]=x (and other scalar-value operations that need
a label key) threw UnsupportedOperationException in the JDBC label
condition builders, which has no webserver error handler and surfaced
as a 500 instead of a 4xx. The value shape (scalar String vs. keyed
Map) determines which operations are actually implemented per
dialect, but that was never validated before dispatch.

AbstractJdbcRepository now rejects a scalar-value labels operation
that requires a key with InvalidQueryFiltersException (400), naming
the filters[labels][OP][key]=value form the caller needs. The
remaining UnsupportedOperationException throws in the six dialect
label builders are swapped to InvalidQueryFiltersException as well,
for direct repository callers.

While tracing the per-dialect operation support, flows' map-value
CONTAINS/NOT_CONTAINS (filters[labels][CONTAINS][key]=value) turned
out to hit the same 500 on all three dialects, even though executions
already supported it - closed by mirroring each dialect's existing
execution-side condition.

subject: feat(dashboards): recycle offscreen dashboard charts and cap their canvas pixel ratio (#18588)
body:
Lazy loading in #18199 stopped dashboards from firing every chart request at once, but it only throttled requests - it never bounded memory. Charts stayed mounted for good once activated, so scrolling a large dashboard grew the number of live ECharts canvases monotonically until the renderer ran out of memory. Large screens hit it first: a canvas backing store costs width times height times the device pixel ratio squared, and a tall viewport activates most of the page in one go, leaving the 200px lookahead doing almost nothing.

Canvas-backed charts (Bar, Pie, TimeSeries) are now unmounted again once their block sits more than 1200px outside the viewport, and remount when it comes back. The gap between that and the 200px activation margin is the hysteresis that keeps ordinary scrolling from thrashing, and a recycled chart's placeholder inherits the height the chart had so content below it does not jump. KPI, Table and Markdown charts are cheap and hold their own page, size and tab state, so they stay mounted once activated.

Chart canvases also render at a pixel ratio capped at 1.5 rather than the full device resolution, which cuts canvas memory substantially on a retina screen for a difference that is not visible on flat fills and thin lines. Activation is spread across frames, four charts at a time, so a tall viewport no longer mounts its whole first screen in a single long task.

Measured on a 30-chart dashboard at 2560x1400 with a device pixel ratio of 2, scrolling from top to bottom: canvas backing store drops from 57.2MB to 10.7MB and live canvases from 12 to 4, while at first paint the canvas cost drops from 19.1MB to 7.3MB. The JS heap is essentially unchanged, which is expected - canvas backing stores are allocated outside the JS heap, and that is the memory the tab actually runs out of.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/14234.
Related to https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/pull/18199.

fix(core): bound Pebble's range() function to prevent heap exhaustion (#18555)
body:
* fix(core): bound Pebble's range() function to prevent heap exhaustion

Pebble's built-in range() eagerly materializes an ArrayList before returning,
so an expression like {{ range(0, 2000000000) }} allocates billions of boxed
entries and OOMs the JVM. Any endpoint that renders a user-supplied Pebble
expression against a real RunContext is exposed, including the execution
eval debug endpoint. BoundedRangeFunction overrides Pebble's range() in
Kestra's Extension bean, computing the requested size upfront and failing
with a bounded PebbleException (surfaced as a normal render error) instead
of delegating once it exceeds 1,000,000 elements.

Closes #18418

* fix(core): bound Pebble render output size to prevent heap exhaustion

Point-fixes such as the bounded range() function and the indent/nindent
filters only close individual OOM vectors one at a time. The underlying
defect is broader: VariableRenderer.renderOnce catches
IOException | RuntimeException, so an OutOfMemoryError produced by any
other unbounded expression (a loop accumulating a huge string, repeated
concatenation, ...) is an Error that escapes rendering entirely and
crashes the JVM.

Guard the output at the writer chokepoint every rendered character flows
through: JsonWriter and TypedObjectWriter now enforce a configurable
kestra.variables.max-output-size (default 10 MiB) and throw a bounded
RenderLimitExceededException once it is exceeded. Because that exception
extends PebbleException, renderOnce maps it to
IllegalVariableEvaluationException - the existing graceful, non-fail-fast
render-failure path - instead of letting an OutOfMemoryError through.

Also centralize the existing single-shot pre-checks (range, indent and
nindent) onto a shared RenderLimits helper using the same exception type.

The Fix with AI entry points (editor validation toast, failed task run, failed execution banner) seeded their prompt into whatever copilot conversation was already active, stacking unrelated fixes in one thread. The seed now carries a contextual thread title and a newThread flag, and CopilotChat drops the active conversation and titles the thread the seeded turn creates when the flag is armed. body:
* fix(flows): make the flows table row navigable on single click

The flows table row had cursor:pointer on the whole row (the standard
"click anywhere to open" affordance) but navigation only fired on
@row-dblclick, so a single click over any non-interactive area (e.g. the
empty execution-statistics/last-execution-date cells of a flow with no
run history) did nothing. KsDataTable didn't forward KsTable's own
row-click event; added that pass-through and wired Flows.vue to it.

Since the selection checkbox and every other still-interactive cell
(namespace link, chart drill-down, Execute button) also live inside the
row, they now stop click propagation so they keep their own behavior
instead of also triggering row navigation.

Closes #18319

* fix(flows): keep modifier-clicks on a flows row from navigating the current tab

RouterLink returns early on a cmd/ctrl-click without calling preventDefault,
so the click still bubbled to the <tr> and the row handler navigated the
current tab while the browser opened its new one. Guard the handler once
instead of per cell: skip modifier and non-primary clicks, and skip clicks
that landed on an interactive descendant. That also covers the EE-injected
extension columns, which cannot stop propagation from this repo.

The per-cell wrappers added for the namespace link, the execution-statistics
chart and the Execute button go away with it; TriggerAvatar keeps its own
stop since its popover reference renders as an image rather than a control.

Assert the KsDataTable forwarding at the component seam so the test no longer
depends on an Element Plus row class name.

fix(plugins): stop inlining icon bytes in the bulk plugin icon indexes (#18586)
body:
* fix(plugins): stop inlining icon bytes in the bulk plugin icon indexes

Cold-loading the Plugins page downloaded ~28MB, 24MB of it the icons
index, and parsing that on the main thread froze the sidebar router,
made the hover border trail the cursor by seconds, and left the page
sluggish until the load settled.

The bytes were never used. Both bulk indexes inline every icon as
base64, but the frontend keeps only the metadata (flowable, monochrome,
hash) and renders each icon from the per-class, browser-cacheable
GET /plugins/icons/{cls}/icon.svg. On a local instance the index is
6.36MB, of which 105KB (1.7%) is that metadata. So the indexes now
answer metadata only; `hash` is non-null exactly when a class has an
icon, which is what the frontend now derives `hasIcon` from. The
metadata view is itself cached, so the served map is a constant rather
than a per-request copy.

Splitting the caches fixes a second bug found on the way: Micronaut
derives a cache key from the method arguments alone, so the two no-arg
@Cacheable("default") index methods shared one key and whichever ran
first served both. GET /plugins/icons/groups was answering the
task-class index -- keyed by task FQCN instead of by plugin group.

Fixing that route exposed one behaviour to preserve: the group index
holds an entry for every group, iconless ones included, and callers read
mere presence as "has an icon". Those entries are now dropped client
side, so an iconless group keeps falling through to the ecosystem
catalog instead of rendering the generic icon.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/issues/10128.

fix(executions): correct Postgres duration sort for executions over one minute (#16909)
body:
* fix(executions): store total duration in milliseconds for Postgres state_duration

The Postgres executions.state_duration generated column used
EXTRACT(MILLISECONDS FROM interval), which returns only the seconds field of
the interval (0-59999) and dropped minutes and hours. Sorting executions by
duration was therefore wrong for any execution lasting one minute or more (a
7m run could sort below a 3m run). MySQL and H2 read the value as total
seconds and were unaffected.

Incremental migration 2.0.11 drops and re-creates the column using
EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM interval) * 1000, backfilling all rows, and recreates the
executions_state_duration index. The statements use IF EXISTS / IF NOT EXISTS
so the migration is safe to replay.

The fresh-install baseline (baseline-postgres.sql) is intentionally left
unchanged: editing it would change the '0-init' migration checksum and break
startup for existing installs (checksum validation throws on mismatch). The
incremental migration corrects fresh installs as well, since it runs on top of
the baseline. A regression test covers durations that straddle the one-minute
boundary.

* fix(executions): rename state-duration migration to 2.0.12

subject: fix: bug-bash quick wins — page=0 SQL leak + Get Started onboarding link (#18552)
body:
* fix(webserver): reject page < 1 with 422 instead of leaking SQL on page=0

Pages are 1-based, and AbstractJdbcRepository maps a page to a SQL offset as
`pageable.getOffset() - pageable.getSize()`, which assumes page >= 1. page=0
produced a negative OFFSET, so the query threw and the raw SQL (table/column
names) was returned in the 500 body — on /users, /credentials and any list endpoint.

Guard page < 1 in PageableUtils.from (alongside the existing size cap) so it is
rejected with a clean 422 before any query is built.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/issues/10223.

* fix(flows): make the "Get Started" onboarding card link to the quickstart guide

The card had an empty link, so OverviewCard rendered a non-clickable <div> with
no icon — clicking it did nothing, unlike its two sibling cards. Point it at the
quickstart guide so it behaves like the others.

Closes #18442.

subject: fix(flows): deduplicate the flow editor's Add-a-trigger panel (#18566)
body:
Clicking "Add a trigger" navigates with ?createTrigger=true, and
MultiPanelFlowEditorView's onMounted handled it by calling
actions.openAddTaskTab directly, bypassing the dedup check that
useNoCodeHandlers.onCreateTask already provides for the same tab type
from the no-code editor's own UI. Every click therefore opened a fresh
tab with a new cache-busted uid, and since panel state persists across
full page reloads (by design), the stale tabs never went away either -
reopening the editor and clicking "Add a trigger" again just piled on
another one.

Routing the call through onCreateTask surfaced a second, latent bug:
its dedup-key computation didn't default 'position' the same way
openAddTaskTab does ("after"), so a caller that omits position (like
this one) computed a key that never matched the tab actually created,
duplicating it every time regardless. Both defaults now agree.

Closes #18321

subject: fix(core): validate and fail-execution on out-of-range user durations (#18549)
body:
Replaces the earlier saturation approach. An unbounded user Duration fed into
Instant/ZonedDateTime.plus() overflowed with an unchecked DateTimeException that
escaped the queue consumer and, under fail-fast, shut the whole instance down
(poison pill).

Two layers:
- Save-time validation: a new @DurationMax constraint (default 10 years) on the
  plain-Duration fields (SLA duration, retry interval/maxInterval/minInterval/
  maxDuration, TimeWindow window/windowAdvance) rejects absurd literals with a 422.
- Runtime guard: DateUtils.plusOrThrow throws a handler-caught InternalException at
  the SLA, Pause and retry arithmetic sites so the individual execution fails
  cleanly and the poison-pill message drains, instead of crashing the executor.
  The flow-trigger window computation is wrapped to log and skip (no execution to
  fail). This also covers Property<Duration> fields (Pause, LoopUntil) that can
  only be checked at runtime, and existing bad flows already on the queue.

Closes #18369
Closes #18421
Closes #18423

Co-authored-by: nKwiatkowski <nkwiatkowski@kestra.io>

subject: fix(flows): return 422 instead of 500 when a bulk-import flow omits namespace (#18575)

unconditionally. A flow source with no namespace: field returns getNamespace() == null,
so the .equals() call NPEs and falls through to the generic Throwable handler as a 500.

Treats a null namespace as invalid up front, alongside the existing mismatched-namespace
check, so it surfaces as the same 422 ConstraintViolationException instead.

subject: fix(core): bound the indent/nindent filters' amount to prevent heap exhaustion (#18560)
body:
AbstractIndent only lower-bounded 'amount' (>= 0) before calling
prefix.repeat(amount), so {{ 'x' | nindent(2000000000) }} allocates a
multi-GB string from a single ordinary task expression and OOMs the
worker. VariableRenderer.renderOnce only catches IOException |
RuntimeException, so the resulting OutOfMemoryError escapes rendering
entirely. Caps amount at 10,000 with a bounded PebbleException above it,
consistent with the already-bounded range() function.

Closes #18365

subject: fix(design-system): apply custom date-range filter with a single bound set (#18554)

subject: fix(executor): fail only the execution when a Loop's values shrinks between iterations (#18564)
body:
* fix(executor): fail only the execution when a Loop's values shrinks between iterations

LoopExecutionEventMessageHandler re-resolves a Loop's 'values' expression
on every iteration but only bounded the next index against the stale
iterationCount captured at loop start, not the freshly-resolved list
size. If a child task shrinks the underlying source (KV, file, subflow
output) between iterations, list.get(nextIndex) threw an
ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException/NoSuchElementException that the handler's
catch clause didn't cover (only InternalException | QueueException |
IOException | FlowNotFoundException). The escaped RuntimeException hit
AbstractSubscriber, which treats any uncaught exception as fatal and
shuts the whole instance down - and redelivers the same poison-pill
message on every restart.

Bounds each re-resolved list/URI read against its actual size, failing
with a clear IllegalStateException when it shrank, and broadens the
catch to RuntimeException so any such user-data issue fails only this
execution instead of escaping to the queue subscriber.

Closes #18355

* fix(executor): fail the loop-values-shrink case via InternalException, not a broadened catch

Keep kestra.queue.fail-fast=true intact. The previous revision broadened the
handler catch to `RuntimeException`, which would also swallow genuine runtime
defects that fail-fast is meant to surface as fatal. Instead, throw the existing
handler-caught InternalException at each shrink/resolution guard so only this
execution fails (via handleFailedExecutionFromExecutor) while any other
RuntimeException still escapes and is treated as fatal. The catch reverts to the
original `InternalException | QueueException | IOException`.

subject: fix(design-system): align alert icon with the first line of wrapped messages (#18547)
body:
Element Plus lays the alert row out with `align-items: center`, so the icon was centred against the whole message block rather than the line it belongs to. Any `KsAlert` whose text wrapped left the icon low by half the overflow: 7px at two lines, 14px at three, 21px at four, and 10.25px for a title with a description. `KsAlert` also set the title to `line-height: 1`, which left wrapped lines with no leading at all.

Anchor the row to the top, restore the title's leading to `--ks-line-height-base`, and raise the glyph by half the difference between the icon box and one line of text so it centres on line one. The offset is derived from whichever element renders the first line, since Element Plus shrinks the title once a description joins it, so there are three cases: title only, title with description, and description only.

Single-line alerts with an icon keep their exact height, since the icon already drove the row's height there. Alerts with a title are 6-7px taller now that wrapped lines have leading.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/18548.
Related to https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/pull/10379.

subject: fix(ci): skip contributor onboarding for authors who already have write access (#18573)
body:
The organization membership check added in https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/pull/18349 never worked. The bot token is scoped to a single repository, so `GET /orgs/kestra-io/members/{username}` answers 404 for every author, and the step could not tell that apart from a genuine non-member. Every author was therefore classified as an outside contributor, and https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/pull/18569 got the "First PR merged" congratulation even though its author is an organization member with private membership. The welcome-on-open comment was skipped there only by luck, because the author had opened a pull request before and the pr_count guard caught it.

This reads the author's repository permission instead. `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}/permission` only needs `metadata: read`, which the repository-scoped installation token already has, and it separates the two populations cleanly: organization members inherit write access on the repository, while outside contributors only ever resolve to `read`. The call is no longer wrapped in a catch, so a token that cannot answer fails the workflow loudly instead of silently commenting on a teammate's pull request.

Related to https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/pull/18349.
Related to https://github.com/kestra-io/docs/pull/5414.

subject: fix(core): render execution-updating task properties for each execution
body:
`SetVariables`, `UnsetVariables` and `Exit` are `ExecutionUpdatableTask`s: the
executor calls `update()` on the task instance held by its cached flow, so a
single task instance is shared by every execution of that flow revision.
`Property` memoizes its rendered value on the instance, so the value computed by
the first execution was reused by all the following ones whatever their inputs —
e.g. a `SetVariables` deriving a boolean from an input kept the boolean of the
first execution.

Skip the render cache in those `update()` methods, like it is already done for
the flowable properties used to compute the next tasks.

subject: fix(core): stop number formatting from crashing for the pt_BR and zh_CN languages (#18395)
body:
getLang() returns the raw stored language code, and the underscore codes pt_BR and zh_CN are not valid BCP 47 language tags, so passing them straight to toLocaleString() made humanizeNumber() throw RangeError: Incorrect locale information provided for users running the UI in Brazilian Portuguese or Simplified Chinese. A new getLanguageTag() helper next to getLang() converts the stored code to its hyphen form (pt_BR -> pt-BR) for Intl consumers, and the html lang attribute now receives the same valid form instead of the raw underscore code. The moment and cronstrue call sites are deliberately untouched: moment wants its own lowercase-hyphen keys (already normalized in init.ts) and cronstrue's locale ids use the underscore form.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/18401.

fallback fell through to Edit flow. Clicking it pushed
flows/update/edit with an undefined id and namespace, so nothing

The fallback is now gated on an existing flow and on creation not

The docs pages already embed the relevant recording, so a "Watch the
video" button on an empty state duplicated that content and drifted out
of sync with it whenever a video was re-recorded or superseded.

`KsEmptyState` loses its `video` prop: `learnMore` is now always rendered
as a "Learn more" button in the actions row, and the subdued arrow link
is gone, so every empty state offers exactly one way to read up on the

was no way to tell which surface sent a reader to a docs page.

and a `utm_campaign` naming the surface. The tags are written out in full
rather than assembled at runtime, since the targets rarely change and a
literal URL is greppable.

`utm_campaign` is the empty-state type rather than the last segment of the
current route as the convention describes. Routes here carry customer data
that has no place in analytics: `/namespaces/edit/<name>` would report a
namespace name, and `/admin/tenants/list` would report `list`.

Entering maintenance mode revoked the per-loop vNode assignments, but exiting
it only resubmitted the loops. As no vNodes rebalance is triggered by a
maintenance toggle, the assignments were never recomputed: the loops idled with
no vNode, and every trigger event was dropped with "Received trigger events for
a non assigned vNode", so already-registered triggers stopped firing and newly
saved flows never registered until the server was restarted.

The assignments are now restored before restarting the scheduling. They are also
distributed over the scheduling-loops that effectively exist instead of over
maxThreads, which orphaned every vNode whose modulo exceeded the number of loops
when a scheduler was assigned fewer vNodes than threads.

Closes kestra-io/kestra-ee#10013

LocalTime fields in the server's default zone, so a flow behaved

to Window/TimeWindow, mirroring Schedule's existing `timezone` property,
so users can pin daily windows to a specific zone.

While extracting the window-boundary computation out of

method, also fix a pre-existing DST bug: the old

resolved to 10:00 or 08:00 on DST transition days. Daily boundaries now
resolve via ZonedDateTime.of(LocalDate, LocalTime, ZoneId), which follows
the JDK's documented gap/overlap semantics and depends only on the date,
the configured time and the zone.

subject: fix(logs): stop a stale search from replacing the logs list
body:
Related to kestra-io/kestra-ee#8205.

Entering `/logs` fired **three** page-sized searches: `KsDataTable` loads on mount, so the first ran against the bare query (no level, no time window — a scan of the whole log table), then the default time range landed, then the default level. Each round also fired 5 level-count probes.

`findLogs` published whatever came back, without checking the response still belonged to the newest search — so the last one to land won. When the broad search is the slow one, its late answer overwrites the correct result: the list shows rows the filters exclude, or nothing when the stale search matched nothing, while every request looks fine in the network tab.

Fix:
- `useRouteFilterPolicy` exposes `isRouteSettled`; `LogsWrapper` gates its first load on it → one search per page entry instead of three.
- The logs store drops superseded responses → covers the races the gate doesn't (filter changes, pagination, refresh).

Two unit specs, both failing on `develop` and passing here. Reproduced in a browser by delaying only the discarded searches: URL says *at or above INFO* (6 lines), list rendered all 9 including DEBUG; now stays at 6.

subject: fix(executions): wait for all WorkingDirectory subtasks before terminating the flowable
body:
A WorkingDirectory runs all its subtasks in the Worker; each reports its
terminal result through an independent queue message. When one subtask
fails, WorkingDirectory (via Sequential/FlowableUtils) resolved to a
terminal state as soon as it saw the failure, without checking whether a
sibling's terminal message had been joined yet. The executor then force-
marked that sibling to the parent's terminal state, discarding its real
outcome and outputs.

This surfaced as a rare flake in WorkingDirectoryTest (t2/t3 output
missing depending on message-join ordering), reproduced on CI independently
of PR #18237, e.g. run 32038144489 on branch refactor/compact-2.0-migrations
a day before that PR existed.

Add a resolveState override on WorkingDirectory that defers to Optional.empty()
while any child taskrun is still non-terminal, so the flowable only resolves
once every reported subtask has actually finished.

JooqDSLContextWrapper and failed on the missing DataSource, since a worker
context drops every datasource bean.

They cannot carry @RepositoryBean itself: it bundles @Singleton, which conflicts
with @EachBean, so they get the server-type condition directly.

subject: fix(flows): normalize the errors refusing to execute a subflow
body:
A flow that cannot be resolved for runtime is carried as a FlowWithException
for two unrelated reasons: it is structurally invalid, or governance blocks
it. Both subflow paths reported "invalid flow", which is wrong and confusing
for the second, and neither can tell them apart today. State neither cause:
the carried message already says which it was.

The Subflow task and the subflow() function now word both refusals, blocked
and disabled, identically and name the flow, which neither disabled message
did and the task's invalid-flow message did not either.

subject: fix(scheduler): report a governance block in the trigger's own logs
body:
A trigger whose flow a governance policy blocks simply stopped firing. The
only trace was a server-side warning the user cannot reach, so the trigger
looked broken with no explanation. Report the block through the trigger's
run context, which is what reaches the UI: per skipped evaluation in the
fetcher, and once per declared trigger at initialization, where a blocked
flow never gets a trigger state and so gets no other report.

TriggerFlowParser now throws FlowBlockedException instead of returning null.
Its old contract encoded three outcomes in one nullable return: the parsed
flow, null for a governance block, and the same instance back for a degraded
parse. A caller could not tell a block from a parse failure, and had no
reason to report either. The checked exception hands over the reason and
makes every caller decide what to do with it.

subject: fix(triggers): expose the flow's labels when rendering scheduled input defaults

execution, so an execution created by a Schedule or ScheduleOnDates trigger

label failed to render.

the executor. Folding the two identical readInputs calls into one is required
for the fix: the second one fed the evaluation result and would otherwise
still render against the un-merged execution.

subject: fix(triggers): do not fail deleting a backfill on a never-evaluated trigger
body:
Deleting a backfill restores the next-evaluation date recorded when the backfill
was created. A trigger backfilled before its first evaluation has none, so the
restore threw a NullPointerException and the delete event was never applied.

Clear the next-evaluation date instead, which makes the scheduler compute a new
one from the trigger definition.

subject: fix(triggers): keep the pre-backfill schedule date when a backfill is paused

nextEvaluationDate on every call. Pausing a backfill re-enters that method while
nextEvaluationDate points inside the backfill window, so the live schedule date
captured at backfill creation was overwritten with the backfill position.
Deleting the backfill then restored that position, and the trigger replayed every
cron slot from there up to now.

Capture the date only when it is not already set, as end and currentDate already do.

Closes kestra-io/kestra-ee#9998

body:
The translations PR gate compared EE leaf keys against OSS leaf keys, so it only caught exact duplicates. It could not see the collision that actually breaks the UI: an EE namespace sitting on a path OSS uses as a message, which the EE-over-OSS merge turns into an object so vue-i18n renders the raw key path - the cause of the lowercase "concurrency" flow tab in kestra-ee.

shadowedOssKeys now reports all three collision shapes (exact duplicate, EE keys nested under an OSS message, an EE message on top of an OSS namespace), each naming the OSS key being shadowed, and the sticky PR comment is reworded since shadowing is fixed by renaming the EE key, not removing it.

fix(core): run queue and KV purges on the executor only
body:
JdbcQueueCleaner carried no server-type guard at all, so every component
of a cluster armed its own hourly timer and ran DELETE FROM queues against
the same shared table concurrently. KVPurgeCleaner was guarded with
notEquals = "WORKER", which still leaves the executor, webserver,
scheduler, indexer and controller all purging the same KV entries.

Both do cluster-global work with no component-local state, so one
component is enough. Introduce @RequiresExecutor — the executor-side
sibling of the existing @WebServerEnabled and @RequiresControllerServer —
and apply it to both jobs. Its defaultValue keeps the jobs enabled when
kestra.server-type is unset, as in tests and runLocal.

Removed from ui/src/translations/*.json:

No EE companion is needed. The deleted EE components read their strings from OSS en.json, so ui-ee/src/translations/ee_translations/*.json has no plugin-defaults keys left and its translations:check is green unchanged.

subject: fix(executions): resolve execution labels in one place, the executor
body:
An execution's labels come from the flow, its triggers, governance policies,
the system, and whoever starts the run. Deciding which of those wins was
spread across every route that creates an execution, and each route had to
remember two things nothing enforced: build from the flow processed for
runtime, and drop the labels a policy pinned. Routes that forgot the first
snapshotted authored labels instead of governed ones. The second was only
ever checked on a single webserver route, so a backfill could still override
a label a policy force-set, and recovering the pinned keys there meant running
the whole policy-enforcement pipeline a second time.

A flow resolved for runtime now carries the label keys an overriding policy
rule force-set, as a ProcessedFlow returned by the parsing service, memoized
alongside the resolved flow and exposed by findByIdForRuntime. ExecutionService
strips those keys from whatever a caller or trigger contributed, so every
Create command is governed identically whichever route built it — backfills
included, which no filter reached before. FlowLabelsResolver, its enterprise
override and the duplicate enforcement pass they needed are removed: the
executor already had the answer.

Executions built outside the Create command, namely subflow tasks and flow
triggers with simple conditions, keep their existing semantics.

subject: fix(executions): evaluate each dependency's own state when following dependencies (#17735)
body:
* fix(executions): evaluate each dependency's own state when following

The pre-scan of already-existing correlated executions in
followDependenciesExecutions passed `current` (the followed execution) to
isStopFollow instead of `exec` (the dependency the loop is emitting for).

As a result, a terminated dependency of a still-running parent was emitted
as "progress" and never removed from `dependencies`, so the stream could
never reach "end-all"; conversely every dependency of an already-terminated
parent was emitted as "end" regardless of its own state.

Add coverage for a partially-terminated graph: a parent that pauses after
its subflow succeeded, so the terminated child must be ended and pruned
while the paused parent only progresses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(executions): de-flake the partially-terminated follow-dependencies test

The 'end-all' assertion depended on live queue delivery: the dependencies
streaming service only resumes its queue subscriber inside registerSubscriber,
which runs after the pre-scan emits, so resuming the parent as soon as the
client observed the pre-scan events could drop its terminal message.

Assert the pre-scan verdicts on the paused graph, then open a second stream
once the graph is fully terminated: the pre-scan alone prunes every dependency
and completes the flux, so no assertion needs a queue delivery.

subject: fix(core): percent-encode '#' and '%' in InternalStorage URI construction (#18058)
body:
* using element plus native splitter el-splitter for resing the side panel

* chore

* fix(core): percent-encode '#' and '%' in InternalStorage URI construction

'#' in a filename was interpreted as a URI fragment delimiter by
URI.resolve(String), silently truncating the stored path and causing
distinct output files to collide and overwrite each other.

'%' was interpreted as a percent-escape start, silently decoding the
filename to a different name; a bare '%' threw IllegalArgumentException.

Fix: replace URI.resolve(String) / URI.create(String) with the quoting
four-argument URI(scheme, host, path, fragment) constructor in all four
putFile helpers of InternalStorage. This follows the same pattern already
established in NamespaceFile.of and NamespaceFileController.toFileUri.

Also update ScriptService.ALLOWED_PATH_CHARS:
- Remove '#': validateStoragePath was green-lighting a name that the old
  URI construction silently mangled.
- Add '%': correctly percent-encoded kestra URIs (e.g. kestra:///path/
  report%231.csv) now survive INTERNAL_STORAGE_PATTERN matching so that
  replaceInternalStorage can resolve them.

Fixes #18051

* fix(core): fix double-encoding of brackets in Download URI and make HttpFunctionTest hermetic

- Remove manual '[' -> '%5B' / ']' -> '%5D' pre-encoding in Download.java;
  InternalStorage.buildStorageUri() now handles all URI-special characters via
  the quoting URI constructor, so pre-encoding caused double-encoding (%255B).
- Remove dead URLEncoder.encode() call (result was never assigned back) and
  clean up the now-unused URLEncoder/StandardCharsets imports.
- Migrate all dummyjson.com external calls in HttpFunctionTest to WireMock
  stubs on localhost:28182 (class already had @WireMockTest) to eliminate
  flaky 429 rate-limit failures in CI.
- Add shouldPercentEncodeBracketsInFilename() to InternalStorageUriTest as
  a regression guard.

* fix(core): re-allow '#' in validateStoragePath now that buildStorageUri encodes it safely

Prior to PR #18058, '#' in a filename was a genuine hazard: URI construction
treated it as a fragment delimiter, silently dropping the filename suffix and
causing distinct files to collide. Removing '#' from ALLOWED_PATH_CHARS was
the right call at the time.

PR #18058 fixed URI construction via the quoting URI(scheme, host, path, fragment)
constructor in InternalStorage.buildStorageUri, which encodes '#' to '%23' in
the path, making 'report#1.csv' store as 'report%231.csv' without truncation.

The same PR also removed '#' from ALLOWED_PATH_CHARS, but that removal is now
wrong: validateStoragePath rejects 'report#1.csv' before it ever reaches
buildStorageUri, causing a task failure for filenames that the storage layer
can handle correctly.

This commit re-adds '#' alongside '%' in ALLOWED_PATH_CHARS, updates the error
message, replaces the now-stale shouldRejectOutputFileWithHash test with an
acceptance assertion, and extends shouldMatchPercentEncodedUriWithInternalStoragePattern
to verify raw '#' URIs are also matched.

* Revert "fix(core): re-allow '#' in validateStoragePath now that buildStorageUri encodes it safely"

This reverts commit 903c0507af84850827ce50150e8cfba8d366bb88.

* revert: restore HttpFunctionTest to original dummyjson.com calls

The WireMock migration was out of scope for this PR. The 429 failure
was a transient rate-limit from the external service, not caused by
the URI encoding changes. Reverting to keep the PR focused.

* test(core): remove useless comments and redundant URI test class

* test(core): restore comments that were inadvertently removed

* reverted commit

fix(core): pin the ZonedDateTime test timezone
body:
shouldWriteZonedDateTimeWithSixFractionalDigits asserted a rendered offset of
+02:00, which only holds where the machine is on Central European Summer Time.
The writer renders in the mapper's timezone, so CI on UTC produced
2024-06-01T10:00:00.123456Z and the expected substring never appeared.

The test now pins the mapper timezone instead of inheriting the machine's, since
the assertion is about the fractional width rather than about where it runs.
Verified under UTC and Asia/Kolkata as well as CEST.

Also realigns a stale JdbcMapper mention in a sibling test comment. The two
remaining mentions live in released migration SQL, which is checksum-validated
at startup and must not be edited.

subject: refactor(core): give Instant and ZonedDateTime one JSON format everywhere
body:
JdbcMapper layered its own Instant and ZonedDateTime serializers on top of
JacksonMapper, so the same value was written one way into a queue message and
another way into the table it ended up in.

The serializers now live in KestraDateTimeModule on the shared JSON mapper:

- Instant keeps the fixed six-digit fraction it already had. The width is
  load-bearing -- the H2 and MySQL generated date columns parse these strings
  with fixed-offset SQL expressions, and MySQL's %f caps at microseconds, where a
  nine-digit fraction makes STR_TO_DATE return NULL.
- ZonedDateTime moves from three digits to six, matching Instant, and now honours
  the context timezone the way Jackson's own serializer does.
- Reading is lenient: any width from zero to nine digits, 'Z' or a numeric
  offset, with a fallback to Jackson's deserializer so epoch numbers and other
  shapes it accepted still work.

ZonedDateTime deliberately keeps Jackson's deserializer: it already accepts any
width.

subject: fix(triggers): accept a widened fractional second in H2 multipleconditions columns
body:
PARSEDATETIME(value, 'uuuu-MM-dd''T''HH:mm:ss.SSSXXX') demands exactly three
fractional digits and fails outright on any other width:

  2024-06-01T12:00:00.000+02:00     -> parses
  2024-06-01T12:00:00.123456+02:00  -> parse error

These two columns read MultipleConditionWindow.start / end, which are
ZonedDateTime. The serializer is about to move onto JacksonMapper and align with
Instant at six digits, so the expression has to stop requiring exactly three
digits first -- otherwise the very next insert violates the NOT NULL constraint.

Normalising the fraction to three digits with a regex leaves the 'Z'/offset
suffix untouched, so the existing 'SSSXXX' pattern keeps handling both forms and
keeps normalising them to UTC on the way into the zoneless TIMESTAMP column.
Verified identical for 'Z', '+02:00', '+05:30' and '-03:30', and independent of
the server timezone.

Truncating to milliseconds is not a regression: the column only ever held
milliseconds, because that is all the three-digit serializer wrote. It is a
filter helper for AbstractJdbcMultipleConditionStateStore, not the source of
truth -- the JSON value is.

subject: fix(executions): build executions from the flow processed for runtime
body:
Every execution creation path (API, webhook, subflow, flow trigger, schedule)
now resolves the flow processed for runtime instead of the flow as authored,
so policy-injected labels and variables are no longer pinned back by authored
values winning the creation-time merge.

Adds FlowLabelsResolver, the single place deciding which caller labels apply
to a target flow (identity in OSS, restricted by editions). Trigger labels no
longer fold in the flow's authored labels, and scheduler metric tags get the
flow labels passed explicitly.

Fixes kestra-io/kestra-ee#9611

subject: feat(worker): warn about the database configuration a worker ignores
body:
A worker opens no database connection, but deployments commonly share one
configuration across every server type. Warn on startup that the inherited
`datasources` and `kestra.repository.type` settings are ignored, rather than
letting an operator believe the worker reads from a database it never contacts.

Part of https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/18001.

subject: fix(worker): never open a database connection from a worker
body:
Micronaut turns every `datasources.<name>` entry into an eagerly-initialized,
fail-fast Hikari pool regardless of `kestra.server-type`. Deployments commonly
share one configuration across all server types, so a remote worker with no route
to the database died at startup on `Failed to initialize pool` for a datasource it
never uses.

Run `server worker` in an ApplicationContext that drops the Micronaut JDBC bean
definitions. The per-datasource `datasources.<name>.enabled=false` switch cannot
be used instead: datasource names are user-chosen, and a command resolves its
property overrides before any configuration is read.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/18001.

subject: fix(worker): never run database migrations from a worker
body:
MigrationStartupRunner was gated on `kestra.repository.type` alone, so a worker
inheriting a shared configuration eagerly acquired the migration lock and applied
the schema migrations at startup. Workers own no repository and reach the cluster
over gRPC, so exclude them.

Part of https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/18001.

subject: feat(flows): cross-resource Source Search across flows, files, KV and secrets (#18041)
body:
* feat(flows): cross-resource Source Search across flows, files, KV and secrets

Extends Source Search from flows-only to a frontend-only cross-resource
scope: flows (source, replaceable), namespace files (path only), KV keys
and secret keys (key names only). Each type gets its own row shape,
preview, and status handling so a slow or failing type never blocks the
others.

- ui/src/stores/crossResourceSearch.ts / ui/src/utils/crossResourceSearch.ts:
  data layer (per-type search, per-namespace file fan-out, status/error
  tracking) — from a prior session, extended here with resourceCountFor,
  files error surfacing, and richer KV metadata (creationDate/expirationDate).
- FlowsSearch.vue: "Search in" pill row (KsCheckTag) with live per-type
  counts/status, "Select all types", flows-only "Flow section" scope,
  cross-resource summary and match navigation, partial-result banners
  (per-type failure, files fan-out progress), and an explicit replace
  exclusion breakdown.
- SourceSearchResults.vue: results grouped by type then by resource, with
  three row shapes (flow line+snippet, file path, KV/secret key) and
  per-namespace retry for failed file searches.
- SourceSearchPreview.vue: flow diff/editor preview unchanged; new
  metadata-card preview for files/KV/secrets stating what wasn't searched,
  with the value always withheld for KV and secrets.

Translated the ~45 new/changed strings into all 12 locales.

* fix(flows): discard superseded cross-resource search results

Each search run now carries a generation; a resolution only writes to the
store while its generation is still the newest. The consumer debounces at
300ms, but lodash's trailing edge only delays invocation, so a slow earlier
run could resolve after a later one and overwrite its results. A namespace
file retry reuses the current generation rather than opening a new one, so
it is discarded once the query has moved on.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(flows): add the missing source_search.type_meta translation key

The type section header rendered the raw key because it was referenced in
SourceSearchResults.vue but never added to any locale. The translations check
only compares other locales against en, so a key missing from en itself is
invisible to it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(flows): surface truncated results and bound the namespace fan-out

The list endpoints cap at 200, so a broad query silently returned a subset
while the counts reported it as complete. Flows is the one replaceable type,
so a bulk replace over a truncated set would have rewritten only part of what
the user believed they had selected. The store now keeps each type's total,
the type header states "first N of M", and replace mode warns before the user
commits.

Namespace files fan out one request per namespace; they now run at most eight
at a time instead of opening one connection per namespace at once.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(flows): pluralise the cross-resource search summary

The summary hardcoded the nouns, so a single-type scope read "1 matches in
1 resources across 1 types". The connector now takes pre-pluralised fragments
and each locale supplies its own word order.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(flows): highlight KV and file matches on the terms the server matched

The KV and namespace-file endpoints split the query into terms and require
each one as a substring, in any order, so `landing.bucket` matches
`landing-bucket-us-east-1` even though that literal never occurs. Highlighting
the whole query then marked nothing and the row read as an unexplained result.

The highlighter now marks the whole query when it does occur verbatim and falls
back to per-term marking only for the rows the term model alone found, so an
ordinary query still renders as one span.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: drop the local dev database from the branch and ignore it

An earlier commit in this branch swept in `cli/data/` while staging with
`git add -A`: a 9 MB embedded H2 database, its trace file, and the namespace
file and KV entries created during manual QA. None of it belongs in the repo.

`cli/data/` is now ignored so a local run cannot stage it again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(flows): bind a namespace-files retry to the query that failed

The retry took the query from the caller, which passed the live search box. A
retry fired after the user edited the query but before the 300ms debounce
re-searched would write results for the new query into a list still rendering
the old one. The store now keeps the query its fan-out ran under and the retry
uses that, so the caller cannot supply a divergent one.

Also drops `anyTruncated`, which nothing consumed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(flows): record translation fingerprints for the source-search keys

develop added a fingerprint sidecar recording the English each translation was
generated from. The source-search keys this branch adds and rewrites were
translated by hand into all 13 locales from exactly this English, so their
fingerprints are recorded rather than regenerated.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(flows): address Source Search review nitpicks and fix story tests

- name the store binding `crossResourceSearchStore` so search/replace on it is
  unambiguous (review nitpick)
- drop the hand-copied i18n message blocks from the two story files and the two
  specs: Storybook's global preview already installs the real `en.json`, and the
  specs now load it directly, so the copy lived in four places (review nitpick)
- collapse the repeated story boilerplate into a single `story()` factory plus a
  shared `allTypesFound` fixture and a `withLoadedFlow` decorator
- register the named routes the preview's "open in …" buttons resolve; without
  them `useLink()` threw and four SourceSearchPreview stories failed
- add `flush-top` to the page section, removing the empty 2rem band the shared
  `section.full-container` padding left between the nav bar and the search header

* fix(flows): count the real selection in the Source Search replace confirm bar

`computeSelectionSummary` built its lookup key as `<namespace>.<id>#<line>:<col>`,
but every key in `selectedMatchKeys` comes from `crossSearchResultKey`, which
prefixes the resource type: `flows:<namespace>.<id>#<line>:<col>`. The `has()`
never hit, so the summary was always `{0, 0}` and the confirm bar read "Replace 0
matches across 0 editable flows" while the diff below it showed 6 matches queued
in 2 flows. Applying was unaffected — `onConfirmReplaceAll` keys correctly — so
only the number the user reads before mutating their flows was wrong.

Build the key with `crossSearchResultKey` so the two cannot drift again, and
cover it in `sourceSearchDiff.spec.ts` (4 of the new cases fail on the old code).

* fix(flows): stop Source Search claiming "no matches" while it is still searching

Typing a query rendered the full-page "No matches for X" state for the whole
300 ms debounce, over a summary reading "0 matches in 0 resources across 0 types"
and pills with no counts — measured live at 40 ms intervals: EMPTY from +50 ms to
+370 ms, then the real results. The skeleton never appeared.

The store cannot tell the two apart: between the keystroke and the first request
leaving, every type is still `idle` and every count still zero, which is exactly
what a finished search that found nothing looks like. So the component now tracks
`searchPending`, set synchronously in the query watcher (before the debounce) and
cleared when the search settles.

The four states were three overlapping booleans that had to be read together with
the template's v-if order to know what rendered. They are now one pure
`searchViewState()` in utils/crossResourceSearch.ts, so the precedence is explicit
and testable; the component just switches on it. Partial results still win over
the skeleton, so the namespace-files fan-out keeps streaming its first hits.

The summary and match-nav are hidden while loading rather than asserting zero. No
new i18n key, so no translation churn.

subject: fix(triggers): remove width dependency in H2 trigger date columns
body:
CAST(LEFT(value, 26) AS TIMESTAMP) on triggers.next_evaluation_date and
last_triggered_date drops the trailing 'Z' only when the stored Instant
carries exactly 6 fractional digits. At any other width the 'Z' survives the
truncation, H2 reads the value as TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE and converts it
into the session timezone on the way into the zoneless column, so the stored
value is shifted by the server's UTC offset and is correct only on a server
running in UTC.

subject: fix(triggers): correct UTC offset extraction in MySQL multipleconditions columns
body:
The generated start_date/end_date columns extracted the UTC offset with
SUBSTRING(v, LENGTH(v) - 5, 5), taking 5 characters where the offset written
by the `.SSSXXX` serializer is 6. `-03:30` became `-03:3`, which CONVERT_TZ
then reads as `-03:03`. The sibling SUBSTRING(v, 1, LENGTH(v) - 6) that strips
the offset off the datetime part already used 6.

Offsets whose minutes part is `00` survived by accident because the dropped
character was a `0`, so only timezones with a non-zero minutes part were
affected: Newfoundland (-03:30), Marquesas (-09:30), India (+05:30), Nepal
(+05:45), Adelaide (+09:30), Iran, Myanmar, Chatham.

subject: fix(core): make GraphUtils topology walk iterative and cycle-safe
body:
GraphUtils.recursiveEdge() had no visited set, so a self-loop in the edge
list made it recurse forever. A task carrying two task runs with the same
values builds two nodes sharing a uid, and the chain edge between them
becomes a self-loop once edges are mapped to uids, so replaying such an
execution overflowed the stack on a four-task flow.

StackOverflowError is an Error, not an Exception, so it escaped the
catch(Exception) in both ExecutionCommandMessageHandler and the queue
polling loop, reached ThreadUncaughtExceptionHandler and exited the JVM. One
replay took down a whole standalone instance.

The walk is now an explicit-stack depth-first search that visits each node
once and reports a node reached twice on the current path as a
CyclicGraphException. It also drops the O(E) rescan of the edge list at
every step in favour of a single index by source.

Output is unchanged: callers only consume the set of reachable edge sources,
which path enumeration and single-visit traversal agree on.

subject: feat(core): parse kotlp OTLP telemetry in TaskLogLineMatcher (#17873)
body:
* feat(core): parse koltp OTLP telemetry in TaskLogLineMatcher

koltp (github.com/kestra-io/koltp) wraps task-runner commands and emits
OpenTelemetry telemetry as OTLP/JSON NDJSON, framed on the console as
::{"oltp":<record>}:: and written bare to files with --log-dir.

TaskLogLineMatcher now parses both shapes: OTLP logs are forwarded to the
run context logger with their original timestamps, OTLP metrics are
converted to Kestra metrics (gauge and cumulative sum to Gauge, delta sum
to Counter, data-point attributes as tags), and OTLP traces are exposed as
POJOs on TaskLogMatch for task-runner implementations without being
consumed by the application. A new public parseOtlp(InputStream, ...)
method ingests bare OTLP NDJSON files line by line, skipping blank or
truncated lines.

* feat(tasks): embed the koltp binary and wrap commands via CommandsWrapper

Adds a Gradle downloadKoltp task that fetches the pinned koltp release
binary into the script module resources, and a KoltpOptions/koltp field
on CommandsWrapper that injects the binary into the working directory
and wraps the final command so its OTLP telemetry flows through the
existing TaskLogLineMatcher.

* feat(tasks): add logFlushInterval option to koltp wrapping

Adds a logFlushInterval KoltpOptions field passed as koltp's
--log-flush-interval, letting long-running commands rotate the
--log-dir NDJSON file periodically. Requires logDir to be set.

* feat(core): forward the OTLP timestamp to Kestra metrics

Adds Counter.of and Gauge.of overloads accepting an explicit
timestamp, and has TaskLogLineMatcher forward each OTLP data point's
timeUnixNano to the resulting metric instead of defaulting to now(),
falling back to the record's instant when it is absent.

* refactor(core): extract parseOtlpLine and widen toInstant visibility

Splits the bare-OTLP-line parsing out of parseOtlp into a reusable
parseOtlpLine method, and exposes toInstant publicly for callers that
need to convert an OTLP timeUnixNano themselves.

* refactor: rename koltp to kotlp and the envelope key to otlp

The wrapper is k + OTLP, so both spellings were letter transpositions. The
upstream repo renamed itself to kotlp and, in the same commit, started emitting
the kjson envelope as ::{"otlp":<json>}:: instead of ::{"oltp":...}::. That
second half is API: a consumer matching on the old key silently stops matching,
with nothing logged. This renames every mention on our side so the two agree.

TaskLogMatch's fifth component is therefore 'otlp', not 'oltp' — EE code
invoking the canonical constructor needs the same one-line update.

kotlpVersion moves to 0.1.0 for the same reason: v0.0.1 predates the rename, so
its release assets are still named koltp and its binary still emits the old key.
The build downloads the binary by asset name, so it has to point at a release
cut after the rename.

* test(core): parse a real kotlp recording instead of a hand-written one

The NDJSON fixture was written by hand from the wire format, so it could only
prove the parser agrees with my reading of the spec. It is now a verbatim
--log-dir recording of kotlp v0.0.1-10-g8072519 — six records over three metric
batches — with only host.name anonymized, so it proves the parser agrees with
the binary Kestra actually ships.

The recording covers what the hand-written one could not: metrics the parser had
never been fed (process.cpu.utilization, process.memory.virtual,
process.thread.count, process.open_file_descriptor.count), the same series
sampled repeatedly so cumulative-sum-to-Gauge collapse is exercised across
batches rather than asserted on a single point, and a closing rusage-derived
batch that keeps process.disk.io at 67108864 rather than restarting at zero.

The three lines that must be skipped — blank, truncated mid-object as rotation
leaves it, and a well-formed object with no OTLP section — are appended after
the recording rather than recorded, since kotlp does not produce them on purpose.

* test(script): pin what the embedded binary and the matcher agree on

Nothing asserted that the binary we embed frames its records the way the matcher
reads them. That gap is the failure mode of the rename: an embedded binary
predating the otlp envelope key produces perfectly valid output that Kestra
ingests none of, with no error anywhere. A run with kotlp enabled now asserts
process.cpu.time reaches the run context, which only happens if both ends spell
the key the same way.

The log-dir test gains the other half. With --log-dir, kotlp treats the file as
the single full copy and prints the child's output raw, so telemetry stops
reaching Kestra through the log lines entirely — the test now states that (no
metrics on the run context) and then feeds the file back through parseOtlp,
which is what a caller setting the option has to do. The javadoc said the option
"mirrors" the records, which reads as both copies being live.

* test: record the fixture from the release the build actually embeds

The previous recording came from a local build of kotlp main, while the version
marker next to the embedded binary already claimed 0.1.0. downloadKotlp skips
the fetch when the marker matches, so the tests ran green against a binary CI
would never use. Re-recorded with the published v0.1.0 asset
(sha256 7f3cdea4898658d8eb53232db8c87b35782896bb42af28b3ed287e7c8b12efd1), which
is also what the script-module tests now execute.

Two documentation corrections found alongside it:

- the fixture javadoc quoted a command that was not the one recorded — it
  dropped the 2>/dev/null and sync, and did not mention --service-name, which is
  where the fixture's service.name comes from. It now quotes the exact
  invocation, so the recording can be reproduced;
- --log-flush-interval does not rotate an existing log.ndjson, it replaces it:
  with the option set there is no log.ndjson at all, only log-1.ndjson,
  log-2.ndjson, ... A caller collecting one fixed name comes back empty, so
  KotlpOptions now says the whole directory has to be shipped back.

The end-to-end envelope-key assertion folds into shouldWrapCommandsWithKotlp-
WhenEnabled, which already had the identical setup, rather than spawning a
second process to assert one more thing about it.

The picker and the dialog each answered the same key press, so closing a
picker opened over the Configure dialog tore the dialog down with it and lost
the pending edits. The dialogs now delegate Escape to the editor's own stack.

* fix(flows): give a locked no-code field the same greyed treatment

A locked string field was only marked readonly, which Element Plus renders
exactly like an editable one, so the flow id looked typeable next to the
greyed-out namespace select even though both carried a lock icon.

* fix(flows): show a task type in the command menu like the picker does

The entries listed their description as the title; they now read name over
description, with the fully qualified name kept searchable behind the scenes.

* test(ui): consume the promise Monaco hands to the ClipboardItem stub

The frontend job went red on unhandled rejections with every test passing:
Monaco's WebKit clipboard workaround cancels the promise it passed to a
previous ClipboardItem, and the stub never consumed it.

* fix(flows): name the lane the picker actually inserts into

Every nested lane announced itself as Tasks because the header came from the
section the lane sits under, so adding a switch case read "Inserting into
Tasks" instead of "Inserting into Case: fast".

* fix(flows): stop the command menu promising a task where it inserts a trigger

Focusing a trigger and opening the menu offered "Insert task after <trigger>",
and running it opened the trigger picker. The target is already named in every
one of these commands, so the noun only had room to be wrong.

* fix(flows): refuse a switch case key the flow already uses

Typing an existing key left Add case enabled, and pressing it quietly aimed at

* test(flows): assert on the open popper, not on any popper in the document

assertion passed on a stale node rather than the one it had just opened.

built-in request fixture inherits storageState, so the BASIC_AUTH cookie rode
along and CsrfTokenFilter demanded an X-CSRF-TOKEN the fixture never sends.
executions.fixture.ts already solved this; the blocks specs never got it.

Verified against a CSRF-enabled backend: 55 failures to 0.

* fix(flows): create a flow-level entry in place, behind a breadcrumb

Adding an input opened a separate tab, which dropped the flow you were
configuring. It now stacks inside the panel with a crumb back to the flow.

The tab could not have saved it either: the task-edit panel only replaces what
already sits at a path, so creation has to go through the segments/Task surface
that inserts. Picking a type now lands the entry in the flow and the form
switches to editing it.

The blocks editor rendered the task-edit panel for creation too, and that panel
only replaces what already sits at a path. With nothing there yet, editingPath
resolved to the bare parentPath, so a create tab wrote the new entry over the
whole section instead of adding to it — reachable from any non-task list and
from the topology's add-task.

Creating an entry had its own presentation — a view stacked inside the flow
properties — so it followed that panel instead of the task-edit preference.
It now takes the same surface as editing a task: the task modal by default,
a tab when tabs are the default, stacked over whatever opened it.

* fix(flows): keep a flow-level creation in the dialog it came from

The creation opened a second dialog on top of the flow one with no way back.
It now replaces the dialog's content behind a crumb, the way drilling into a
nested field already does, and still falls through to a tab when tabs are the
task-edit default.

On an empty instance the post-login redirect lands on the AI Copilot page, where
the product tour auto-starts. auth.setup then parked that guided card in the
storage state every project inherits, so its overlay swallowed clicks: 10 blocks

body:
* refactor(iam): read basic-auth login state from a server-issued cookie

The UI tracked basic-auth login state with a sessionStorage flag it set
itself after a successful /login round-trip, separate from the actual
HttpOnly BASIC_AUTH session cookie. That flag could drift from the real
session (e.g. a failed logout request, a new tab, a browser restart).

The server now issues a second, non-HttpOnly cookie in lockstep with
BASIC_AUTH on login/setup and clears it on logout. It carries no
credentials, only mirrors whether the session cookie is set, so the UI's
isLoggedIn() can read it directly instead of maintaining its own flag.

Also drops the redundant BasicAuth.signIn() call in the setup flow: it
only existed to set the old sessionStorage flag, since addBasicAuth()
already logs the user in via the server response.

* test(iam): remove basicAuth.ts unit tests

* Apply suggestions from code review

Co-authored-by: Barthélémy Ledoux <ledouxb@me.com>

* fix(iam): drop logout() HttpRequest param to keep the EE override compiling

kestra-ee's MiscController overrides logout() with no arguments
(@Replaces the OSS class and returns notAllowed() there, since EE logs
out through Micronaut Security instead). Adding a HttpRequest param to
the OSS logout() broke that @Override and failed the EE build.

The flag cookie is cleared without a secure() attribute on logout, same
as the existing BASIC_AUTH cookie clear just above it.

* refactor(iam): drop stale comment in BasicAuthSetup.vue

* fix(triggers): avoid Lombok builder type in Webhook method signatures

The plain javadoc tool (unlike compileJava) doesn't run Lombok's
annotation processor, so it can't resolve Output.OutputBuilder when it
appears as a parameter or return type — only as a local variable type,
where the compiler has already inferred it inside a fully-attributed
method body. This broke :core:javadoc after the webhook body/multipart
feature introduced withBody()/withMultipartBody() with that signature.

Inline both helpers into Webhook#evaluate() so the generated builder
type is only ever used as a local variable, never in a signature.

body:
* chore(deps): upgrade monaco-editor to 0.56.0

monaco-editor 0.55/0.56 restructured its ESM export map: deep imports
drop the `esm/vs` prefix (e.g. `monaco-editor/editor/editor.api`), the
side-effect-only `editor/editor.all` entry point was replaced by the
tree-shakeable `features/register.all`, and the deprecated
`languages.typescript`/`languages.json` namespaces are replaced by the
top-level `typescript`/`json` exports from
`monaco-editor/languages/features/*/register`.

Update every deep import across the app, design system and topology
package accordingly, patch monaco-worker-manager (used transitively by
monaco-yaml) which still imports the old `esm/vs` path, and drop the
now-obsolete monaco-editor patch (the source-mapping-url line it
stripped no longer exists in the upstream bundle).

monaco-editor now calls the native `CSS.escape()` API for class-name
sanitization, which jsdom doesn't implement; polyfill it in the jsdom
test setups that mount Monaco-backed components.

* fix(assets): fix CI failures from the monaco-editor 0.56 upgrade

- monaco-editor 0.56 defaults to the native EditContext API instead of
  a hidden textarea for keyboard input. That surface isn't a real
  <textarea>/[contenteditable], which broke Playwright's .fill() (and
  other tooling built on the old input model) in the flow-input E2E
  test. Opt KsEditor back into the textarea-based input explicitly.
- Extend the existing monaco teardown-race rejection filter to also
  match monaco-yaml's "Missing requestHandler or method" errors from
  its debounced findLinks/getCodeAction worker calls racing a story's
  editor disposal - same non-actionable class as the already-filtered
  "Canceled: Canceled" rejections, just matched by message since the
  rejection crosses the worker postMessage boundary before it's seen.
- Force dompurify (bundled by monaco-editor) to ^3.4.13 via an
  override - 0.56 vendors dompurify@3.4.8, which has several disclosed
  XSS-adjacent CVEs fixed in later patch releases.
- Deduplicate the CSS.escape() jsdom polyfill (needed because
  monaco-editor 0.56 now sanitizes via the native API, which jsdom
  doesn't implement) into a single tests/unit/monacoCssEscapePolyfill
  module instead of copy-pasting it across every test setup file.

* fix(assets): fix monaco-yaml's link/code-action worker calls on 0.56

Root-caused the "Missing requestHandler or method: findLinks/getCodeAction"
storybook CI failures: monaco-editor 0.56 requires an `esmModuleLocation` on
the descriptor passed to `monaco.editor.createWebWorker({createData, label,
moduleId})` whenever it has to construct the worker itself. monaco-worker-manager
(and any MonacoEnvironment.getWorker-based setup, ours included) never provides
one, so `createWebWorker` silently falls back to an in-process no-op worker
whose foreign module is always null - every RPC call to it, not just
findLinks/getCodeAction, rejects the same way; those two just happen to be the
ones whose callers (Monaco's own link/code-action contributions) don't swallow
the rejection.

Patch monaco-worker-manager to build the worker itself via
MonacoEnvironment.getWorker/getWorkerUrl and pass it in already-primed with the
same ignore-message-then-createData handshake monaco-editor's own first-party
workers use (internal/common/workers.js), so `createWebWorker` takes the
"already a Worker" fast path instead of needing esmModuleLocation.

Verified directly against a running Storybook with Playwright (bypassing this
sandbox's broken vitest browser-mode Chromium revision): the unpatched package
reproduces the exact CI error, the patched one doesn't.

Drop the message-based rejection filter added in the previous commit - it was
a shot in the dark at masking what looked like a teardown race; this fixes the
actual bug instead, so filtering it is no longer needed.

subject: fix(executions): read the execution without ACL after an async operation
body:
Triggering an execution in a distributed deployment returned 404 "Execution
disappeared after create", while the execution itself ran to completion. The same
applied to every endpoint that waits on an async operation: restart, resume,
pause, kill, force-run, label and status changes.

awaitBlockingAction waits for the AsyncOperationProcessedEvent, then reads the
execution back to return it. AsyncOperationWaiter completes its sink from
AsyncEventStreamingService's queue-polling thread, so that read does not run on
the request thread and has no authenticated principal. The ACL-enforcing
findById fails closed when no namespace is allowed, returns empty, and the
endpoint reports the execution as missing.

That is why it only showed in distributed mode, and only where namespace ACLs are
enforced: standalone completes the operation without crossing a queue, and
without ACLs the lookup returns the execution regardless of principal.

Use findByIdWithoutAcl, as ExecutionStreamingService already does for its own
queue-polling reads and for the same reason. This is not a new authorization
decision: the endpoint that submitted the operation already authorized the caller
on the request thread, and this only reads back the execution it just acted on.

Fixes #17863

flowHaveTasks() used a single regex with a lazy [\s\S]*? capture plus

backtracking on crafted flow sources.

id:/id : field, either inline or on a following line.

contradicting the comment above it. Move the boundary scan into phase
1 so it genuinely determines both bounds of the tasks: block, and
phase 2 only scans within those known bounds looking for a task item.

Addresses review feedback on kestra-io/kestra#18013.

in one pass instead of a findIndex followed by a separate for loop.
