fix(ci): welcome first-time contributors again (#17996)
body:
The contributor onboarding job has been failing on every external pull request with `Must have push access to view repository collaborators`, so nobody has been welcomed.

With `skip-internal-contributors: true`, `plbstl/first-contribution` first checks org membership and then falls back to `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{username}`, using the same `GH_READ_ORG_TOKEN` for both. That endpoint requires push access, which a `read:org` token does not have — exactly the scope the action's README tells you to create — so GitHub answers 403. The action only swallows 404s and rethrows everything else, which aborts it before it can comment. That path is reached for every author who is not an org member, which is precisely the audience the workflow exists for.

GitHub already resolves the author's relationship to the repository and ships it in the `pull_request_target` payload as `author_association`, so internal contributors are now filtered out in the job condition and no token is needed at all. The remaining logic — has the author committed here before, is this their first pull request — runs on the built-in `GITHUB_TOKEN` through `actions/github-script`, which also removes a third-party action holding `pull-requests: write` in a `pull_request_target` job.

The congratulations message is wired up for the first time as well. It was configured as `pr-merged-msg` but could never fire: the workflow only listened for `opened`, and the action's merged path passes `author` to `issues.listForRepo`, whose parameter is `creator` — so it compares the repository's oldest pull request against the one just merged, and never matches.

The job now declares the permissions the API calls actually need: `contents: read` to read the author's commit history and `issues: read` to read their issues and pull requests, alongside the existing `pull-requests: write`.

build(core): run e2e tests on pushes to develop (#17804)
body:
The push trigger targeted `main`, which does not exist in this repository — the default branch is `develop` — so the "on merge" half of the original change never fired and the suite only ever ran from cron or manual dispatch. It now triggers on `develop` and `releases/*`, so a merge gets its own E2E signal with per-commit attribution instead of waiting for the next scheduled window.

Because the suite now runs per merge, add a concurrency group: without one, back-to-back merges each start a full build-from-source of the product and stack up. Successive runs on the same ref now supersede each other instead.

Thin the schedule from every two hours on weekdays down to a single nightly run. The working-hours runs mostly re-tested a commit the push trigger had already covered; a nightly run keeps what the schedule genuinely adds — flakiness on an unchanged commit, and external drift such as base images or plugin downloads on days with no merges — and extends that to weekends.

Adding `releases/*` to the push trigger had no effect on any release branch that exists today: for a push event GitHub reads the workflow file from the branch being pushed to, and every current release branch carries its own copy of this file. The glob would only ever have applied to release branches cut from develop after this landed, which is a behaviour change not worth making implicitly. Giving the existing release branches their own E2E-on-merge coverage is a backport of this commit, decided per branch.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/issues/9662.

subject: build(core): let the translation generator finish inside the CI job timeout (#17794)
body:
The scheduled auto-translate workflow has been failing continuously and could not recover on its own. Every missing key was translated in its own request, awaited one at a time, and the twelve languages were processed one after another, so wall-clock time was the sum of every call. Once the backlog passed roughly 250 keys a full run no longer fit in the job's ten minutes, and because each run restarts the whole backlog from scratch the failure fed itself: the job was cancelled before committing anything, the backlog grew, and the next run died in the same place.

The backlog that broke it was 117 missing keys in each of 12 languages, so 1404 requests, which took about 54 minutes.

Four changes, measured against the prompts this script actually sends.

Requests now go through a gate that admits at most TRANSLATION_CONCURRENCY of them at once, defaulting to 10 and overridable for local runs. The gate wraps the single point of network I/O rather than each loop, so languages, keys and locale files can all be scheduled freely while the number of simultaneous requests stays bounded by one shared budget.

Keys within a language, the languages themselves, and the design-system locale files are now requested together instead of in sequence.

The thinking pass is switched off. Translating a short UI string needs no deliberation, and thinking was the dominant cost: median latency drops from about 2.5s to about 0.5s with it disabled, and on the sampled strings placeholder handling stayed perfect while reserved-term handling improved slightly. Newer models were measured too and are not the answer here — gemini-3.6-flash was the slowest of the candidates at about 4.1s.

The changed-key set is memoised per input file. It depends only on en.json, yet it was recomputed for every language, running `git fetch --all` and re-parsing two revisions of the file twelve times over.

Ordering is unchanged. Translations are collected into a dictionary keyed by translation key and the output is assembled afterwards in en.json order, so completion order cannot influence the file. For the locale files the language blocks are likewise assembled after the fact, `en` first, because the serialised output preserves key order and letting completion order decide it would rewrite the whole file on every run.

Verified by running the previous and new versions against a deterministic stub whose latency varies per string, so completion order is deliberately shuffled: with 100 keys translated across four languages all fourteen output files came out byte-for-byte identical, while the logs confirm the two runs completed in different orders. A live run of 120 keys across all twelve languages took 9.5s with no errors, no empty values and no placeholder drift in anything it produced; the same work sequentially with thinking enabled would have taken about 5 minutes. Extrapolated to the 1404-key backlog that broke CI, a full run is now roughly 2 minutes against the unchanged ten-minute budget.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/17791.

subject: fix(core): repair broken interpolation placeholders in translated UI strings (#17831)
body: * fix(core): use single-brace interpolation placeholders in translated UI strings vue-i18n interpolates single-brace placeholders (`{tool}`); a double-brace one is a hard compile error — `t()` throws `Message compilation error: Not allowed nest placeholder` rather than degrading to literal text, so any component rendering an affected key fails outright. Seventeen keys had drifted to `{{...}}` across the twelve non-English locales, most of them on the AI copilot surface (`ai.copilot.context.*`, `ai.copilot.toolResult.*`, `ai.copilot.draft.applyConfirm`, `ai.copilot.toolCall`) plus `mcp.servers_count`, `trigger enable dialog.bulk title` and `resume from breakpoint title`. Only the brace syntax changes here — the translated wording is untouched. * chore(core): drop the unused top-level select translation key `select` ("Select your {{section}}") was added by a bulk key import in #7509 and never wired up: no `t("select")`, `$t("select")` or `keypath="select"` anywhere in kestra/ui/src, kestra/ui/packages, kestra-ee/ui-ee/src, ui-libs/src or docs/src, and every dynamically built key is prefixed (`no_code.select.${blockType}`, `ai.copilot.toolResult.${outcome}`, `${key}.title`) so none can resolve to it. It was also the one double-brace placeholder present in en.json itself, which is what the generator then propagated to all twelve locales. The nested `no_code.select` and `dependency.search.namespace.select` keys are unrelated and stay. * docs(core): correct the placeholder brace syntax in the translation generator prompt The Gemini prompt told the model that placeholders are enclosed in double curly braces and used "System {{label}}" as the worked example, so the model faithfully "normalised" the single-brace placeholders it was given into double-brace ones — which is what produced the seventeen broken keys fixed in the previous commit. The EE generator already described them as `{label}` and has no such breakage. Both the prompt and the mirrored rule in AGENTS.md now state the single-brace syntax, name the compile error double braces cause, and require the translation to carry exactly the placeholder set of the English source. * fix(core): realign translated UI strings with the placeholders their English source declares Six keys interpolated a different set of variables than en.json, so they rendered wrong even though they compiled: - `pluginPage.search` invented a `{count}` the English string never had ("Search across 1400+ plugins"), so all twelve locales rendered an empty gap where the number should be — "Suche in + Plugins". - `filters.save.name_already_used` (de) likewise invented `{label}`. - `replay confirm` (ko) and `trigger enable dialog.options.follow` (hi, ja) dropped the `{id}` / `{property}` the English source passes. - `last X days count`, `date range count` and `date count` (hi) had the placeholder names themselves translated into Hindi — `{गिनती}`, `{दिनों}`, `{तारीख}` — which vue-i18n rejects outright with "Invalid token in placeholder". The affected values were emptied and regenerated through `translations:generate` with the corrected prompt rather than hand-edited. The Korean `replay confirm` came back wrapping the id in backticks; it is aligned to the `{id}` the other twelve locales use. * build(core): fail the translations check on uncompilable messages and placeholder drift `translations:check` only compared key sets, so it stayed green through every bug fixed in this branch: seventeen keys that made `t()` throw, and six that silently interpolated the wrong variables. Two checks are added to the shared comparator, which EE also runs via `ui-ee/src/translations/check.ts`: - Every message — English included — is run through vue-i18n's own `baseCompile`. That is the ground truth for whether `t()` throws at render time, and it is what flags `{{name}}` ("Not allowed nest placeholder") and non-ASCII placeholder names ("Invalid token in placeholder"). - Every translation must interpolate the same placeholders as its English source, so an invented or dropped variable fails instead of rendering as an empty gap. Placeholder names are compared as a set, so a locale that collapses `{count} item | {count} items` into a single plural form still passes, and `{'literal'}` escapes are excluded since they are text rather than interpolation. * fix(core): drop stray NUL bytes from the translations comparator Two literal NUL bytes had slipped into the placeholder-set comparison, in place of the spaces the join was meant to use. The check behaved correctly — NUL is a perfectly good delimiter — but the file was no longer valid text, so git classified it as binary and GitHub rendered "Binary file not shown" instead of the diff. The join is replaced with an element-wise comparison, which needs no delimiter at all and cannot collide with a placeholder name whatever it contains. * fix(core): treat backslash-escaped braces as literal text in the placeholder scan `\{` and `\}` are how a message renders a literal brace — `variable_explorer.one_key` is `"\{ 1 key \}"` and comes out as "{ 1 key }". The placeholder scanner did not know about that escape and read `1 key \` as a placeholder name. Nothing failed because of it: the reading was wrong in the same way for English and for every translation, so the sets still matched. It would have surfaced the moment a locale translated the words between those braces. Only `{'...'}` literal blocks were being stripped before scanning; backslash escapes are now stripped too. * style(core): use a plain string for the non-interpolated EN comparison header The header line was written as a template literal but interpolates nothing, which trips the eslint `quotes` rule. Flagged by reviewdog on #17831. * build(deps): restore develop's ui lockfile in the merge commit The merge commit reverted ui/package-lock.json to its pre-merge state, dropping the entries develop's dependency update added, so `npm ci` failed the frontend and build-artifacts jobs with "Missing: unrun@0.3.1 from lock file". This branch changes no dependency and does not touch ui/package.json, so develop's lockfile is authoritative and is restored verbatim. The net diff against develop is now the sixteen files this PR means to change. Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/17839.

subject: fix(executions): show the BOOL input toggle as on when its default is true (#17941)
body:
`Input.defaults` is a `Property`, which serialises as its expression string, so a `defaults: true` on a BOOL input reaches the form as the string "true". el-switch compares `modelValue` against `activeValue` by identity, so "true" !== true: it emits `update:modelValue` = false during its own setup, which turns the toggle off and also runs the form's change handler. That change bumps the validate generation, so the in-flight response carrying the real default is dropped as stale and the follow-up round-trip submits `false` — the toggle is then off for good and the execution runs with the wrong value. Coerce the BOOL default to a real boolean in `normalize()` so the switch accepts it.

This affects the flow execute form and, through the same shared `InputsForm`, the EE Apps `CreateExecutionForm` block.

This is a regression: the identical fix landed on `releases/v1.3.x` as 6265761bfa (for https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/issues/8978) but never reached `develop`. Both a helper-level unit test and a component-level test that mounts the real switch (no stub) now guard it — the component test reproduces the reported symptom, including the stale-response round-trip that makes the toggle stay off.

`normalizeForComponents` was a near-duplicate of `normalize` with no callers anywhere — not in `ui/src`, `ui/tests`, `ui/packages`, `kestra-ee/ui-ee` or `ui-libs`. It had already drifted from the function it mirrors: it checked `value === null` first (so a null BOOL yielded `undefined` rather than `false`) and never grew the `MULTISELECT`, `JSON` and `YAML` branches `normalize` gained later.

Keeping it meant every normalization rule had to be written twice, which is precisely how the BOOL default coercion in the previous commit goes missing again — someone fixes the copy they landed on and the two diverge. Delete it instead, and drop the test that pinned the two in lockstep.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra-ee/issues/9772.

subject: fix(core): stop logging an ECharts deprecation warning on every chart render (#17837)
body:
ECharts 6 deprecated `grid.containLabel`. When it is set to `true` without registering the optional `LegacyGridContainLabel` module, ECharts logs "[ECharts] Specified `grid.containLabel` but no `use(LegacyGridContainLabel)`;use `grid.outerBounds` instead." and silently falls back to the new `outerBounds` layout path, so every dashboard, sparkline and chart panel polluted the browser console.

Migrate to the `grid.outerBounds*` API instead of reviving the deprecated code path:

- `containLabel: true` becomes `outerBoundsMode: "same"`, which resolves to the same `rawGridRect.clone()` outer bounds that ECharts already fell back to internally after logging the warning, so the rendered layout is unchanged.
- `containLabel: false` in compact/sparkline mode becomes `outerBoundsMode: "none"`, the direct expression of "do not reserve space for axis labels", keeping the grid at its explicit 2px-inset rect.

`outerBoundsContain` is left at its default `"all"` (axis labels plus axis names) rather than the legacy-equivalent `"axisLabel"`: no affected chart sets an axis `name`, so it behaves identically today while also handling axis names correctly if one is added later.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/17836.

subject: fix(ci): fail the contributor onboarding workflow when the welcome action errors (#17939)
body:
The action's `fail-on-error` input defaults to false, so any error inside `plbstl/first-contribution` is logged as an annotation and the step still exits 0. With `skip-internal-contributors: true` the org-membership check runs before anything else, and a non-404 response is re-thrown — so an expired `GH_READ_ORG_TOKEN` aborts the action before it can react or comment, while the job still reports success.

That is exactly what has been happening: every run in the retained log window returns `Org membership check returned status: 401 / Bad credentials`, meaning no first-time contributor has been welcomed for weeks behind a green check.

Setting `fail-on-error: true` does not fix the credential, but it makes the breakage visible instead of silent.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/17940.

subject: feat(cases): QueryFilter/JDBC support + UI foundation for Cases (EE) (#17504)
body:
* feat(cases): QueryFilter Cases companion + design-system polish

- QueryFilter Resource.CASE/CASE_TEMPLATE + Field.SEVERITY/ASSIGNEE for the EE Cases feature
- Executions/Overview extension-point bridge for EE cases integration
- demo/Cases.vue upsell page + route + menu teaser for OSS users without the EE feature
- KsSelect/KsOption colorMap mechanism (severity/status badge coloring)
- KsSegmented icon slot forwarding for the Cases list/board view toggle

fix(cases): drop LABELS from CASE queryable fields, fix ACL-scoped flow lookup in test loader

Cases replaced labels with typed custom fields; LABELS filtering on CASE is
no longer meaningful. AbstractLoaderExtension now resolves loaded flows
without an ACL check so @LoadFlows fixtures work under any namespace,
including system-namespace flows used by Cases' attached actions.

* feat(executor): notify on task pause via PausedTaskNotifier extension point

EE Cases feature auto-notifies assignees when a HumanTask task pauses; needs an OSS extension point since ExecutorService lives here.

* fix(ui): NProgress counter leak, SDK dev-server false-positive, unrun dep, KsOption padding

* fix(sdk): widen client-facade error interceptor's response type to Response | undefined

Drops the undefined-as-unknown-as-Response cast in the network-error catch path now that the interceptor's error.fns signature accepts the real type.

* fix(executions): integrate EE's extra columns into the native column-picker

extraColumns rendered unconditionally as its own KsTableColumn block, bypassing
optionalColumns entirely - its header showed even for tenants without the
feature, and it couldn't be hidden via the same picker as native columns.
Merge it into optionalColumns instead, sourced from a getExtraColumns()
function (was a static array) so EE can return an empty list when disabled.

Also fill in the Cases entry in the empty-state links registry, which was
still a bare placeholder.

* feat(pebble): support blocking functions, not just masking, in PebbleEngineFactory

Masking still invokes the delegate before hiding its result, which is fine for
a pure read like secret() but not for a function with a real external side
effect. Add a functionsToBlock param that drops a function from the engine
entirely instead, reusing the existing drop mechanism from createRestricted().
The 2-arg overload delegates with an empty block list, so existing callers
are unaffected.

* fix(query-filter): scope supported operators per resource, not just per field

Field#supportedOp() was one shared list per field across every resource
that declares it, so widening it for one resource's need (Cases needing
IN/NOT_IN on STATUS) silently widened it for every other resource sharing
that field too — even when that resource's backing store can't honor the
wider op set. Invitation's STATUS is virtual (ACCEPTED/PENDING map to the
status column, EXPIRED is computed from expired_at), so it can't support a
single-column SQL IN/NOT_IN the way Case's real status column can.

Adds Resource#supportedOp(field), defaulting to the field's own list and
overridden for INVITATION to reject IN/NOT_IN on STATUS. Threaded through
the two other call sites that already had the resource in scope:
AiToolSpecifications' per-field AI tool schema and QueryFilterToolExecutor's
per-field validation.

* fix(executor): keep task-lookup inside the best-effort notifier try/catch

findTaskByTaskId() was called outside the try/catch meant to make the
paused-task notifier call non-fatal, so a lookup failure would still abort
the pause instead of just being logged like a notifier failure.

* fix(kestra-sdk): make dev freshness check single-flight and restore fetch stub in tests

* fix(executions): gate optional table columns via condition

subject: fix(ui): re-trigger the error toast for every new message, not just t… (#17880)
body:
* fix(ui): re-trigger the error toast for every new message, not just the first

ErrorToast.vue only ever built and showed its KsNotification from an
onMounted hook, which fires once when coreStore.message first goes
from empty to set. Nothing reset coreStore.message afterward and
nothing watched the message prop, so any second error while the
first toast was still open (duration: 0, never auto-hides) silently
never appeared.

Move the notification build into a watch(() => props.message, ...,
{immediate: true}) so it re-fires on every new message, closing any
previous notification first. Also close the notification on unmount,
since coreStore.message can be reset to falsy elsewhere (e.g.
FlowRun.vue), which unmounts this component via the parent's v-if
without ever telling the notification library to close its popup.

Closes #17871

subject: fix(executions): show and submit multiselect values whenever the execute form is prefilled (#17326)
body:
The MULTISELECT field binds a different model from the one the execute form submits, so every path that seeded one without the other left the control and the payload disagreeing. Replaying an execution filled the payload but rendered an empty field; a flow-declared default or a server-rendered value rendered a filled field that submitted nothing; and a trigger's stored inputs got both wrong at once, showing nothing while submitting a comma-joined string instead of a JSON array. All of those paths now go through a single helper that writes both models.

A MULTISELECT `defaults` reaches the browser JSON-encoded as a string, because `Property` serialises that way, so it is now parsed into an array before it reaches the select instead of being rendered as one tag containing raw JSON text.

Replaying an execution no longer prefills a SECRET input at all. `Execution.inputs` holds the serialised `EncryptedString` object rather than the plaintext, so prefilling it put `[object Object]` in the password field and submitted that literal string to be re-encrypted as the new secret, running the flow with a silently wrong value. The field is now left empty for the user to re-enter.

Two storybook stories cover the rendered control and the submitted payload together; both fail without these changes.

The BOOLEAN case in the linked issue needs no change: `BOOL` already prefills correctly, and `BOOLEAN` is not a valid input type. Only the backend's inability to decrypt a replayed secret keeps the issue open, which is why this does not close it.

Closes https://github.com/kestra-io/kestra/issues/3523.

subject: fix(worker): declare a real gRPC retry policy for replay-safe RPCs
body:
`max-retry-attempts` only capped a retry policy that was never declared, so
it had no effect and a controller lost mid-call failed the task. Metadata
reads and execution-log reads now retry on UNAVAILABLE; every other RPC stays
excluded, either because a replay is unsafe or because an outer layer already
owns the retry, and a test fails until a newly added RPC is classified either
way. Health check and retry share one service config, since a second
defaultServiceConfig call replaces the first.

The attempt count moves next to the settings it belongs with, as
`kestra.grpc.channel.retry.max-attempts`, and its default drops from 10 to 4
now that attempts are real. It still feeds the channel-level ceiling as well
as the policy, so the ceiling can never silently truncate the policy. The gRPC
spec requires at least 2 attempts, but rather than refuse to start on a lower
value, anything below the minimum leaves retries off.
